card.name: Comma after non-anion gap
card.fires_on: The comma right after "non-anion gap" in the carbonic anhydrase inhibitor warning, just before "hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis". It also fires weakly on a few other spots where a fixed medical phrase continues.

modes.label: Comma before hyperchloremic
modes.description: The comma after "non-anion gap" in the warning about serum bicarbonate decrease with carbonic anhydrase inhibitors.
modes.example: frequently causes a decrease in serum bicarbonate and induce non-anion gap<<,>> hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis

modes.label: Other fixed phrase continuations
modes.description: Isolated words inside set medical phrases, such as "referred to as" before a condition name or the end of "episodica" in a contraindication list.
modes.example: the condition is referred to<< as>> reflux laryngitis.

card.plain: It marks the spot in a very familiar warning sentence where the next words, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, are almost certain.
